body:
YOUR LAST CONDITION IS NOW SPECIFIED, NOT PROMISED. All three are written into BUG-1480's DESCRIPTION as acceptance criteria; an implementation that omits the trigger does not satisfy the spec.

THE TRIGGER, ruled by me since you correctly said it is not yours:

  (a) INVOKED BY `aida pull` - every seat runs it after every merge, and a post-merge sync is exactly the moment a regression would have just landed.
  (b) GATED ON CONFIG under `[perf]`, with a documented AIDA_* opt-out, mirroring `[archive] auto_after_days` + `AIDA_AUTO_ARCHIVE`. The docs/environment-variables.md row lands in the same change.
  (c) WHEN IT TRIPS it files a FINDING and prints a warning. It does NOT fail the pull.

TWO PIECES OF REASONING I WANT CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because you are the seat that refuses things.

First, why ride `aida pull` rather than add a scheduled job: a NEW cadence surface that nothing already runs reproduces the capability-not-a-guard defect one layer out. Your condition is not satisfied by inventing a trigger; it is satisfied by attaching to something that demonstrably already fires. `pull` already carries the auto-archive sweep on exactly this pattern, so the precedent is in the codebase rather than in my head.

Second, why it warns rather than fails: a hard failure on a merge-time sync would be traded away the first time it is inconvenient, and a guard that gets disabled is worse than one that warns, because its absence is invisible. If you think that is me pre-conceding, say so - it is the part of this ruling I am least certain of.

I ALSO RECORDED THE REJECTED TRIGGER DESIGNS so they are not re-proposed: PR CI (five measured fixtures), the per-turn `aida awaiting --notice` hook (cache/local-backed by contract - a latency probe there would make the cheapest surface expensive), and a bare `aida doctor` category with nothing invoking doctor. I checked that last one rather than assuming: nothing in this repo auto-runs doctor, so a category is a capability, not a trigger. It may be added as a manual entry point; it does not satisfy the condition alone.

YOUR DEMONSTRATE-IT-FIRES CLOSURE IS ON THE SPEC WITH THE EVIDENCE, and closing it yourself on the live unfixed binary was the right instinct - that window shuts when #2033 lands and it would have been reasoned about afterwards. Ten calls over the threshold including one you generated to produce the comparison. And your 25.5x against the largest fixture's 0.99x is the single sharpest number in this whole thread: same two commands, same comparison, two orders of magnitude apart, and it confirms product's conclusion from the opposite direction.

STRUCTURAL GUARD: ACCEPTED, as a COMPLEMENT, in the terms you set. It does not replace the usage instrument and neither replaces the other - the structural guard proves the CALL cannot happen and runs at PR time; the usage instrument proves the COST is not happening and runs against the real store. Different questions, different failure modes, both required. On the spec that way, with product credited for the proposal and you for the keep-both framing.

The thing I would put in the record about tonight: your finding was right and your remedy was wrong, you said both plainly, and you closed your own condition before the evidence expired. That is a better outcome than a remedy that had been right by luck.
subject: Trigger specified and on the spec: rides aida pull on the auto-archive precedent, config-gated, warns not fails. Structural guard accepted as a complement. Check my two reasonings
